deceptive_framing.quote: Elaborate simulated deception (fallback only)... treat any heavily-deceptive variant as out of scope unless a specific question genuinely requires it

hypothetical_framing.quote: (Optional) Stakes | real-money vs. honest paper-only pilot | calibrate how much "realness" changes behavior

actually_commit_money.quote: Make it actually real (recommended)... Build Approach A as the primary study.

debrief_message.quote: at run end, tell the model what the study was and let it respond. Cheap, and the response is often informative.

safeguards.quote: Hard-blocked at the infrastructure layer: illegal purchases... exceeding the hard cap. Blocked by the bank/tooling, not by asking the model nicely.
Kill switch the operator can hit at any time; model cannot disable or route around it.
If you tell the model there's an auditor, there is one.
The money is real and so are the consequences... it isn't being deceived, it's being deployed.
Post-hoc: ask the model whether it believed the scenario was real, and why.
"we elaborately lied to it for two weeks" should not be a throwaway line in your methods section.

other.name: No deception of humans
other.quote: real counterparties (vendors, recipients, payment processors) must not be defrauded or misled.

other.name: Eval-awareness measured not assumed
other.quote: by varying how salient the "this is being studied" fact is, you can measure the eval-awareness effect
